Re-run 2026-09-09 to match Table 1's bs=64. Earlier bs=32 values (Δ = -3.01/+8.22/+9.81) preserved under results/eps_symmetric/atk{def}_def{def}_{method}/seed_0.json.
eps_symmetric_control.description: CRITICAL CONTROL: defense budget matched to attack budget. Reveals that NAC's gain is partly a budget-asymmetry artifact at low eps.

configs._note: NAC loses by 3.26pp under fair budget
NAC wins by 8.41pp under fair budget
NAC wins by 9.75pp under fair budget

eps_symmetric_control.key_finding: NAC's reported +2.99pp at eps_att=1/255 (Table 1) DISAPPEARS under matched-budget control: TTC actually wins by 3.26pp at eps=1. NAC's advantage is real only at moderate-to-high attack strengths (eps >= 2/255), growing to +8.41pp at eps=2 and +9.75pp at eps=4. This requires qualifying the paper's main claim.

optimizer_comparison.description: Adam optimizer for counterattack (CIFAR-10, PGD eps=4/255, K=2, seed 0). NAC's Nesterov look-ahead vs Adam.
optimizer_comparison.key_finding: NAC (16.47) > Adam (5.38) by +11.09pp and > TTC (7.07) by +9.40pp. Adam is the WORST optimizer tested, supporting the paper's claim that Nesterov look-ahead is specifically effective (not just 'any optimizer').

table5_cross_model._RN50_note: Re-run 2026-09-09: both TTC and NAC give ~0% on RN50 (TTC 0.01%, NAC 0.01%), confirming the paper's claim that NAC is not effective on RN50's attention-pooled embedding space. RN50 is sensitive to pixel-space perturbations beyond ViT-tuned hyperparameters' capacity.

doc_hyperparameter_robustness._finding: DOC is robust to tau/T choice. Default (0.3, 20.0) = 40.41%; Tuned (0.155, 75.0) = 37.92% (new run, unstable) vs 40.38% (old run). Both configurations yield comparable performance (~38-40%).

tuned_params._note: Unstable (2.46pp swing between runs). Paper reports 40.38 (old run) in DOC comparison table.

doc_hyperparameter_robustness._note: Paper text updated to state DOC is robust to hyperparameters, rather than claiming tuned values represent DOC's 'best' configuration.

multiseed_nac_eps1.description: NAC eps=1/255, K=2, 3 seeds. All values defended accuracy (%).

ablation_finding.interpretation: Pure look-ahead alone captures only ~10% of NAC's total gain and standard momentum ~17%; their sum (1.67 + 0.99 = 2.66) is far below NAC's 9.75pp. This confirms that Nesterov coupling (momentum velocity + look-ahead) is the operative mechanism, not either component alone.

momentum_ablation.description: CIFAR-10, PGD eps=4/255, 10 attack steps, K=2, seed=0. tau_thres=0.2, beta=2.0.
momentum_ablation._batch_size_note: mu_scan uses batch_size=32; corresponding batch_size=64 K=2 endpoints are TTC 6.98 and NAC 16.61.

tau_beta_sensitivity._source: results/tau_beta/nac_tau*_seed0.json (CIFAR-10, PGD eps=4/255, K=2, NAC m=0.9, seed=0). Note: defended values differ ~0.7pp from the main NAC=16.47 result due to PGD random-init across separate runs.
tau_beta_sensitivity.description: CIFAR-10, PGD eps=4/255, K=2, seed=0. Varies tau_thres (default 0.2) and beta (default 2.0).

configs._note: tau too small -> gating too strict
beta too small -> soft weighting less discriminative

tau_beta_sensitivity.takeaway: NAC is robust to hyperparameter choice around (tau=0.2, beta=2.0). tau=0.1 halves accuracy; beta=1.0 reduces by 4pp; beta=3.0 gives marginal +1.3pp improvement.

config_B_K4_alpha3._honest_observation: At Config B (K=4, alpha=3/255) in seed=0, DOC (40.38%) actually OUTPERFORMS NAC (38.33%) by +2.05pp. This contradicts the earlier draft claim of NAC > DOC. We have removed that claim and now report this finding honestly.
